scope: Observed monthly active-workforce headcount and mean-salary extrapolation, census identity/status integrity, source calendar-month semantics, pay comparability, model selection, finite output, and fail-closed history validation.
confirmed_findings_fixed: Invalid or missing historical SnapshotDate values were silently dropped, allowing incomplete censuses to remain forecastable.
Conflicting employee records within the same selected census could raise an uncaught exception instead of returning a governed unavailable result.
Timezone conversion could move a source census into the previous calendar month and corrupt the monthly series.
Salary forecasts could compare months with incomplete or shifting measured-salary coverage.
Headcount forecasts could proceed without EmployeeID identity reconciliation and could fail with a low-level KeyError.
Unknown employment/attrition status rows could silently disappear from monthly active headcount and create false workforce trends.
Constant historical series unnecessarily invoked Holt-Winters and emitted numerical divide-by-zero diagnostics instead of deterministically using the last-observation baseline.
The isolated forensic workflow initially omitted a transitive Pydantic dependency; the workflow was corrected without changing engine semantics.
A same-month latest-census challenge fixture initially used the same date as the existing census; the fixture was corrected to test the intended contract.
interpretation_boundary: Forecasts are descriptive extrapolations from complete observed monthly censuses. They are not causal predictions, staffing recommendations, or guarantees. No prediction interval is claimed unless independently implemented and validated.
remaining_scientific_limits: A complete census cannot be proven from row contents alone; source-system export completeness remains an organizational data-governance assumption.
Forecast validity under structural breaks, reorganizations, acquisitions, policy changes, and macro shocks requires real prospective validation.
Model-selection validation uses only the last three observed months and does not establish long-horizon calibration.
